audience.text: Python developers who need programmatic PowerPoint generation and editing without rendering or conversion.

capabilities.text: Open, create, and save .pptx files while preserving unknown XML parts verbatim.
capabilities.title: Presentation I/O

capabilities.text: Add, remove, clone, and reorder slides; insert auto shapes, picture frames, tables, connectors, and group shapes.
capabilities.title: Slide and shape management

capabilities.text: Format text at portion, paragraph, and text frame levels, including font properties, bullets, and hyperlinks.
capabilities.title: Text formatting

capabilities.text: Create 73 chart types backed by embedded XLSX workbooks with full series, categories, and data point control.
capabilities.title: Chart creation

capabilities.text: Apply 57 transition types with per-slide timing and advance settings.
capabilities.title: Slide transitions

capabilities.text: Set core, app, and custom document properties including title, author, and version.
capabilities.title: Document properties

capabilities.text: Add speaker notes to slides and insert comments with authors, positions, and timestamps.
capabilities.title: Notes and comments

capabilities.text: Embed images from bytes or file-like objects using add_image and add_picture_frame.
capabilities.title: Image embedding

limitations.text: Only seven SaveFormat values produce valid output; fourteen raise ValueError instead of writing mislabeled files.
No rendering or conversion to PDF, HTML, XPS, or image formats is supported; this is a design boundary.
Presentation sections, slide size configuration, SmartArt, OLE objects, VBA macros, and encryption are not implemented.
add_image requires image bytes or a file-like object, not a file path.
Comment threads authored in PowerPoint may lose resolved status, @-mentions, and reply chains when saved.
Assigning to a non-existent property raises AttributeError rather than silently ignoring.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic creation and modification of PowerPoint presentations using pure Python code.
Supports embedding rich content such as tables, charts, images, connectors, and group shapes into presentations.
Allows preservation of unknown XML parts when loading and re-saving presentations, preventing data loss.
Provides support for document properties, speaker notes, comments, and slide transitions for complete presentation authoring.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Python is an open-source Python library for creating, reading, and editing PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations.

uncertainties: The exact set of 24 Markdown dialects supported for export is not specified in the facts.
Whether the library supports reading non-.pptx formats beyond what is implied by the input format facts is unclear.
The behavior of the library when encountering malformed or corrupted .pptx files is not documented in the facts.

workflows.name: Edit existing presentation
workflows.text: Load a .pptx file, modify slides, shapes, or text, and save the updated presentation.

workflows.name: Add shapes and formatting

workflows.name: Export to Markdown

workflows.name: Add slide transitions
